# MCP (Model Context Protocol) Gotchas

> Known Model Context Protocol server/host integration patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Process-global MCP server leaks across tenants if run in-process](process-global-server-cross-tenant-leak.md): A stdio MCP server whose state is a process-global client built from process.env must be spawned as one child per session in a multi-tenant host; sharing it in-process leaks one tenant's data to another. HIGH.
- [Partial credential update silently wipes OAuth-captured hidden keys](partial-credential-update-clobbers-oauth-keys.md): Rebuilding a connector credential from visible form fields only deletes OAuth-captured keys (refresh token, realm id) on any re-save; merge stored non-field keys forward instead of replacing. HIGH.
- [A missing MCP tool is not a missing capability](missing-tool-vs-missing-capability.md): "Defined" is not "advertised" -- a tool can be written, exported and deployed while never being named in the list the server returns from tools/list, so no client can see it and nothing errors; grepping the source gives a false negative. Meanwhile the route it wraps usually still accepts X-API-Key, so enumerate every transport before accepting a workaround. HIGH.
- [A tool description that calls a missing feature a filter hides the gap](description-frames-missing-feature-as-filter.md): "excluded by default" asserts a switchable default and therefore promises a parameter; when none exists and no other tool provides the data, readers conclude they cannot find the flag rather than that the feature was never built. The backing table, service layer, REST route and dashboard UI had all shipped -- only the MCP tool was missing, so the description was the one place the gap could surface and it described it as a setting. Grep descriptions for "by default"/"excluded"/"unless" and require each to name the parameter or the tool. MEDIUM.
- [A streamable-HTTP session and its stdio child live until the client sends DELETE](session-and-child-leak-without-delete.md): StreamableHTTPServerTransport has no TTL -- onclose fires only from close(), reached only from an explicit DELETE, and a dropped SSE stream does not end the session. Any client that just vanishes pins its session forever, and for a stdio provider that pins a spawned child process too. Those children live outside the V8 heap, so the container is OOM-killed with exit 137 and NO "JavaScript heap out of memory" banner -- the absence of that banner is the tell that this is the cgroup killer, not a JS heap leak, and heap profiling chases the wrong thing. Idle children burn no CPU, so metrics stay flat until the kill. Stamp lastSeenAt per request, sweep on an unref'd interval, cap sessions before spawning, and drain on SIGTERM. HIGH.
- [MCP-Protocol-Version is present three revisions before the rules it appears to gate](protocol-version-header-predates-its-rules.md): The header arrived in 2025-06-18; the `_meta` envelope and Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name it must agree with arrived in 2026-07-28. Gating the strict rules on the header's PRESENCE 400s every 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 client about `_meta` fields its revision never defined -- which is most clients shipping today. Presents as "connected, but couldn't load tools": the handshake succeeds and every tools/list is refused. Gate on the VALUE, and exempt `initialize` (2026-07-28 has no handshake, so calling it means the handshake era whatever header was sent). HIGH.
- [A 404 for an unimplemented method kills pre-2026 MCP clients](unknown-method-404-kills-legacy-clients.md): 2026-07-28 requires 404 + -32601 for an unimplemented method, but for 2025-03-26..2025-11-25 a 400/404/405 on the endpoint is the signal to fall back to the deprecated HTTP+SSE transport -- which a modern-only server does not serve, so the client GETs, gets 405, and dies over a method it was merely probing for. Answer 404 only in the modern era. Separately, an unknown TOOL is a bad parameter (200 + -32602), not a missing method, and a refused tool is a successful result carrying isError, never a JSON-RPC error. HIGH.
- [A protected resource must not advertise offline_access](protected-resource-must-not-advertise-offline-access.md): RFC 9728 `scopes_supported` means the minimal set needed to reach THIS resource, so `openid` (an AS authentication scope) and `offline_access` (a client/AS refresh concern) do not belong there or in the WWW-Authenticate challenge. Not a hard failure, so it survives review while misinforming clients. The same challenge SHOULD carry a `scope` hint, without which clients request everything advertised. Send the challenge only for authentication failures -- a suspended account cannot fix itself with a fresh token and will loop. MEDIUM.
- [The MCP TypeScript SDK v2 is separate packages -- @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is the v1 line](sdk-v2-replaces-hand-rolled-protocol.md): `npm view @modelcontextprotocol/sdk` returns the v1 monolith built on Node req/res, which looks like it needs bridging on a fetch stack and invites hand-rolling the protocol. v2 is `@modelcontextprotocol/server` plus `/client`, `/core` and framework adapters; `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` is Request-in/Response-out, `createMcpHandler` builds a fresh server per request (per-caller tools/list, no cross-tenant state), `authInfo` is strictly pass-through, and `fromJsonSchema` reuses existing JSON Schema without a Zod rewrite. MEDIUM.
